svg.title: Graph construction — okfy algorithm explainer
svg.desc: How the loaded file set becomes the drawn graph. One pass builds the skeleton. Every directory a file path implies gets a dir node, collected from the paths, sorted and created root-down, so a missing ancestor is created with its child; a directory that holds only files still gets its own node, so a folder of assets is not left loose at the bundle root. The kind comes from the name: index.md at any depth is an index, any other Markdown file is a concept, and anything else is a file, which the graph never parses for links. Each node then hangs off its directory with a tree link. There are five kinds: Directory, Index file, Concept, File and Tag. A concept takes the colour of its OKF type and falls back to purple; a tag hub shares the Directory colour. Only index and concept nodes get links, and their targets come from the body's Markdown links and from the frontmatter's sources, at most 256 sources per file. A target that is already loaded becomes one ref link, drawn curved with an arrowhead. A non-Markdown file becomes a visible placeholder node, drawn at half opacity with a dashed ring and fetched only when it is opened. An embedded image is drawn inline in the preview and gets no node, unless the image is already a loaded file. Markdown that is not loaded is kept as missing and loaded on demand when clicked. One ref link exists per concept-and-target pair, a concept is never linked to itself, and a mutual pair keeps two links but draws one straight edge with an arrowhead at each end. Tag hubs are built only while the tags toggle is on or a tag filter is active: one hub per tag and per namespace prefix, so a/b nests under a, namespace to child namespace is a solid link, a node to its leaf tag is dashed with the arrowhead at the hub, and a top-level hub is a child of the root with no link of its own. Every directory and tag hub gets an ordered neighbour list — child directories, then index files, then concepts, then files — and a page saying how many are drawn. A directory opens with its whole skeleton, every child directory and index file plus up to 50 concepts, so its files are held back; a tag hub opens fully unless it has more than 16 neighbours, when it opens one page of 8; the bundle root always opens fully. The expansion dial, opened by pressing and holding a node, changes the page, and a page set by hand survives a rebuild. A search or a filter is a lens that draws the whole subtree anyway. Graph size is capped at 32 000 nodes and 80 000 links, and a graph that would exceed the caps is rejected whole, so a bad bundle can never replace a good one.
svg.text: OKFY · ALGORITHM EXPLAINER
Graph construction
One pass over the files: directories, kinds, links and the page each node shows
1 · From files to nodes
bundle
docs/
assets/
index.md
guide.md
logo.png
assets/ has no Markdown of its own
One pass over the files
A dir node for every directory a file path implies,
created on demand, so a missing ancestor comes with it.
index.md anywhere → index.
Any other Markdown file → concept.
Anything else → file, and it is never parsed for links.
Each node hangs off its directory with a tree link.
Directories are collected from every file path, sorted, then created root-down, so the node
tree always matches the folders, and one that holds only files still gets its own node.
2 · The five kinds
A node's kind is decided when the graph is built
Directory
one node per directory a file path implies
Index file
a file named index.md, at any depth
Concept
any other Markdown file, coloured by its OKF type
File
anything else; an unloaded placeholder keeps this kind
Tag
a hub per tag, built only while tags are shown
Concept colour comes from the OKF type: Reference, Guide and Agent Skill each have one,
and an unknown type falls back to purple. A tag hub shares the Directory colour.
3 · Reference edges
Where a reference comes from
The body's Markdown links, and the frontmatter's sources[].resource — up to 256 per file.
What the target becomes
loaded in the file set
one ref link, drawn curved with an arrowhead
a non-Markdown file
a placeholder node; its bytes are fetched only when it is opened
an embedded image
drawn inline in the preview and given no node, unless the image is already loaded
Markdown that is not loaded
kept as missing, and a click loads it on demand
One ref link per concept-and-target pair, deduplicated, and a concept is never linked to itself.
A mutual pair keeps two links, but draws one straight edge with an arrowhead at each end.
4 · Tag hubs
bundle
#a
#a/b
guide.md
A hub per tag and per namespace prefix
#a/b nests under #a, and a namespace hub needs no file.
namespace to namespace, solid
a node to its leaf tag, dashed
A top-level hub is a child of the root, with no link of its own.
Hubs are built only while the tags toggle is on or a tag filter
is active; otherwise the graph is unchanged.
5 · Partial expansion
docs/
3 shown, 2 held back
children: directories, index files, concepts, then files
A directory opens with its whole skeleton: every child
directory and index file, plus up to 50 concepts.
Its files stay held back, so a folder of assets does
not flood the graph.
A tag hub opens fully unless it has more than 16
neighbours, when it opens one page of 8.
The bundle root always opens fully.
A page you set by hand survives the next rebuild.
The expansion dial, opened by pressing and holding a node, changes the page. A search or a
filter is a lens that draws the whole subtree anyway, so a match is never held back.
Graph size is capped at 32 000 nodes and 80 000 links. A bundle that would exceed the caps is
rejected whole, so a bad bundle can never replace a good graph.
